Aryan practised distinguishing points, line segments, lines and rays by endpoints; some identifications were right but not steady yet.
Aryan practised naming segments, lines and rays with letters; ray AB was identified as starting at A, including in a direction example.
Aryan practised that a line is not a different or bigger line when drawn longer; they continued to describe drawn length as measurable.
Aryan practised identifying a line segment from two endpoints and a finite portion.
end.parentNote: Asha practised endpoints, arrows, and naming rays with Aryan. They used useful examples such as torchlight and correctly stated that ray AB starts at A, while also mixing up whether the visible length of a line changes the line itself; this was not corrected by the last seen response. At home, ask Aryan to label one segment, one line, and one ray, then say which endpoints or arrows each has.
